hypothesis: Realized-rate changes account for more of Summit Field’s matched-period sales movement than sold-unit volume.
test: Run the exact SKU × channel Shapley bridge and compare absolute rate, volume and mix contributions.
falsifier: The rate contribution is smaller than volume or reverses the headline direction.
scope: All business; current versus comparison dates.
metric_basis: Sales before returns; integer-cent reconciled bridge.
limitation: The generator adds $3 to regular prices in 2025, but discounts and mix also affect realized rate. This is not price elasticity.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Summit Field’s October–December markdown share is higher than its other observed months.
test: Aggregate markdown / effective regular merchandise sales by calendar month; compare Q4 only when both Q4 and other months are in scope.
falsifier: Observed Q4 markdown share is not higher, or the selected dates lack a valid comparison.
scope: Selected sale dates, monthly, all divisions and channels.
limitation: Q4 10% unit markdown is a documented construction rule; rounding and product weighting affect the observed ratio.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: The App price book is lower than Web and POS for the same SKU/quarter universe in the selected interval.
test: Compare overlapping price intervals across all channels; the generated assortment covers the same SKU/quarter cells. Inspect counts before comparing.
falsifier: The price-book averages are equal/higher for App or the SKU/quarter universes differ.
scope: Price intervals overlapping the selected dates; unweighted price-book comparison.
metric_basis: Effective regular price per SKU/channel/quarter, before markdown or promotion.
limitation: The generator sets App $1 below other channels. This tests the price book, not the observed basket ASP or customer response.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Web and App Apparel/Footwear sales have higher observed unit return rates than Store POS in the same sale cohorts.
test: Compare returned units / original sold units separately for Apparel and Footwear by channel.
falsifier: Digital unit return rates are no higher than POS or a base is too small to compare.
scope: Apparel and Footwear; selected original sale dates; all linked returns.
metric_basis: Unit return rate on fully observed 60-day sales cohorts.
limitation: The generator uses 17% digital versus 9% POS line return probability. One returned unit per selected line means unit return rates need not equal those probabilities.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Damaged returns reduce merchandise margin more per returned unit because they recover no product cost.
test: Compare recovered_cost_cents by return reason on selected original sales cohorts; inspect actual reason labels.
falsifier: Damaged return rows recover cost, or no damaged returns are observed in scope.
scope: Returns linked to selected original sales; all observed return dates.
metric_basis: Refunded merchandise and recovered cost, positive stored cents.
limitation: Non-damaged returns are restockable by construction. This excludes processing, shipping and labor costs.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Returned merchandise and recovered COGS explain a material difference between original sales growth and cohort merchandise-margin growth.
test: Reconcile original net sales − refunds − original COGS + recovered COGS in both periods.
falsifier: Return-related component deltas are immaterial and the gap is explained by other accounting components.
scope: All divisions; matched original sale cohorts.
metric_basis: Cohort merchandise margin after all observed returns.
limitation: Accounting attribution does not identify causes of returns or measure operating profit.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Pooling customer_key 0 as a real buyer would distort Summit Field’s repeat and customer-reach analysis.
test: Measure anonymous versus identified orders and sales; confirm distinct identified buyers exclude 0.
falsifier: No anonymous orders are present in scope.
metric_basis: Order/sales coverage by identity; anonymous key 0 excluded from buyer counts.
limitation: The generator targets 28% anonymous orders. It is not legitimate to infer anonymous-customer loyalty or repeat behavior.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Loyalty-attached orders have different observed AOV and unit baskets from unattached orders.
test: Compare header-based sales / orders and units / orders for loyalty_key > 0 versus 0.
falsifier: Differences in basket measures are immaterial under a stated business threshold.
scope: Selected completed orders; loyalty attached versus not attached.
metric_basis: AOV before returns; no header-to-line fan-out.
limitation: Enrollment and attachment are synthetic selection rules. Differences do not measure the loyalty program’s impact.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: The newest first-observed purchase cohorts appear weaker if incomplete 90/180-day windows are treated as non-repeat.
test: Inspect eligible_90 / eligible_180 and compare repeat only among customers with mature observation windows.
falsifier: All compared cohorts are fully mature and the proposed maturity artifact cannot explain the difference.
scope: Identified buyers; first observed purchase in selected dates; history through selected end.
metric_basis: Repeat on a later date within 90/180 days; mature eligible denominator.
limitation: History is left-censored at 2024-01-01. First observed is not proven acquisition, and same-day repeat orders are excluded by the existing recipe.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Outdoor unit share rises in June/July, Footwear in August/September, and Apparel in November–January within the observed calendar.
test: Compare monthly division-unit shares, using all-division monthly units as the denominator; inspect both years when available.
falsifier: The expected division-share pattern is absent or dates do not cover the relevant and adjacent months.
scope: Selected sale dates; monthly division groups.
metric_basis: Original sold units and sales before returns.
limitation: These are explicit seasonal preferences in the generator, not newly discovered real-world consumer preferences.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: The private-label group has different cohort margin and unit-return rates from other brands.
test: Classify using v_product.is_private_label; calculate margin / cohort realized sales and returned / original units.
falsifier: Differences are negligible or attributable entirely to division/product composition in follow-up tests.
scope: Selected sale cohorts, all channels, private-label flag rather than a guessed brand name.
metric_basis: Cohort realized revenue, merchandise margin, original and returned units.
limitation: Brand assignment is synthetic. Group comparisons mix product composition and do not measure brand preference.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Loyalty-only and channel-restricted campaigns produce different redeemed sales and discount exposure across POS, Web and App.
test: Measure redeemed lines, units, net sales and promotion discount by loyalty_only and actual order channel.
falsifier: No material exposure difference is present, or the scope lacks both campaign types.
scope: Redeemed sale lines with promotion_key > 0 in selected dates.
limitation: Campaign eligibility, timing on days 10–24, and 60% eligible redemption are generator rules. No randomized holdout supports causal lift.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: POS, Web and App contribute differently to the sales movement because order counts and average baskets move differently.
test: Compare matched header-based order totals, units and AOV by channel; reconcile sales to the overall headline.
falsifier: Channel contributions and within-channel basket changes do not explain the measured movement.
scope: Matched sale periods; digital selling_store_key 0 kept separate from POS stores.
metric_basis: Header net merchandise sales and AOV before returns.
limitation: The generator targets 66% POS, 23% Web, 11% App. Differences do not measure channel effectiveness.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Completed orders per observed day are higher on weekends than weekdays in Summit Field.
test: Compare order count divided by observed calendar-day count, split by dim_date.is_weekend.
falsifier: Weekend orders per observed day are no higher, or holiday/month composition explains the difference in a follow-up.
scope: Selected sale dates; weekend versus weekday.
metric_basis: Completed orders per day; not foot traffic or conversion.
limitation: The generator adds weekend sampling weight; control month composition for a like-for-like comparison.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Pickup, DC shipping and ship-from-store orders have different basket sizes and observed return rates.
test: Inspect order totals, original sales, sold units and linked returned units by fulfillment method; distinguish carry-out.
falsifier: Observed differences are immaterial or disappear within channel/division strata.
scope: Selected completed sale cohorts; all observed returns.
metric_basis: Original sales / orders for AOV; cohort returned units / original units.
limitation: Only promise dates exist. This cannot test on-time delivery, delivery cost or causal retention effects.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: Some divisions carry more available inventory relative to observed SKU sales rates, despite all generated locations stocking every SKU.
test: Compare latest completed available balances with selected-period units per week; inspect zero-sale SKUs separately.
falsifier: Comparable weeks-of-supply differences are small or high stock is proportional to observed sales.
scope: SKU totals over all locations; latest completed snapshot on/before selected end.
metric_basis: Available units / observed sales units per week; not a sum of weekly inventory balances.
limitation: Receipts are generated to cover sales. The model has no daily stockout, unmet-demand or actual replenishment lead-time process.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: The latest inventory balance is explained by opening stock, receipts, sold units, restockable returns and shrink.
test: Verify opening + receipts + restocks − sold − shrink = closing at the latest completed snapshot.
falsifier: A nonzero reconciliation residual appears; investigate data or aggregation errors before interpreting performance.
scope: One latest completed Monday–Sunday snapshot; division totals.
metric_basis: Stock/flow reconciliation in units; available = closing − reserved.
limitation: This is a data-integrity hypothesis. Passing does not prove optimized stocking or absence of intraday stockouts.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.

hypothesis: One of Apparel, Footwear, Team Sports, Outdoor, Golf or Fitness accounts for a disproportionate share of the matched-period sales change.
test: Rank division dollar contributions by absolute size and reconcile their sum to the header-based total change.
falsifier: Contributions are broadly distributed and no division is material under a declared threshold.
scope: Six merchandise divisions, matched dates, all channels.
metric_basis: Original merchandise sales before returns, current minus comparison.
limitation: Divisions locate where change occurred. They are not independent causes and should not be added to overlapping channel/brand decompositions.
provenance: Summit Field METRICS.md, MODEL.md, executable playbooks and verified catalog; Milky Way deck is a workflow reference only.
